title: Rock The Country Fest Organizer Peachtree Entertainment Reportedly Shuts Down
summary: Peachtree Entertainment has shuttered and laid off staff, according to reports.
contentText:
Nashville-based music promoter Peachtree Entertainment, the organizer behind the Rock The Country festivals, has reportedly shut down and laid off staffers. The news was first reported by Decibel .

A statement released Friday (Nov. 20) to Loudwire from the city of Decatur, Ala., which hosted Rock The South, noted that the city had “received word that Peachtree Entertainment has decided to cease operations and close its business. This was a significant and unexpected development for City leadership.”

In the statement, the City of Decatur also noted it is reviewing its five-year agreement with Peachtree Entertainment and “assessing what this decision means for Decatur and the future of Rock the South.”

The statement added, “Because the review is ongoing, the City cannot confirm 2027 festival or event dates at this time. We can say that no city funds have been exchanged for the 2027 contract year. We understand that residents, local businesses, festival fans and community partners will have questions. The City will share additional information once we have verified facts and a clearer understanding of the available next steps.”

Representatives for Peachtree Entertainment have not responded to Billboard ‘s request for comment.

In January, Peachtree announced this year’s eight-city run of Rock the Country festivals, with stops in states including Florida, Georgia, Texas and Michigan. Rock the Country’s lineup initially listed performers at various shows including Kid Rock, Jason Aldean, Blake Shelton, Jelly Roll, Brooks & Dunn, Hank Williams Jr., Lynyrd Skynyrd, Brantley Gilbert and more.

Rock the Country came under fire earlier this year after backlash due to the festival’s perceived political ties. Some artists, including Carter Faith, Shinedown and Morgan Wade, exited the fest’s lineup, while a July 25-26 show in South Carolina was ultimately canceled.

Peachtree Entertainment was founded in 2013 by Bradley Jordan . The company’s event portfolio expanded to include Rock the South, Rock The Country, Furnace Fest, Bulls, Bands and Barrels and more. Jordan now co-manages Ella Langley with Megan Hinde through Painted Rock Entertainment.

In 2024, Peachtree Entertainment partnered with LiveCo and hired Nathan Baugh as CEO and Shane Quick to spearhead artist relations and live events.

Earlier this month, Peachtree Entertainment president of live events Quick announced his departure from Peachtree. Quick founded the Alabama country music festival Rock the South in 2012.

According to TicketNews , LiveCo divested its ownership stake in Peachtree in 2025 and said in a statement offered to TicketNews that it “has had no ownership interest, governance role, or operational involvement in the company since that time.”

Peachtree has also been involved with past and/or current tours for Alan Jackson, Josh Turner, Hudson Westbrook and Hunter Flynn.
